title: Model Switchover & Fallback: Triage Runbook for Enterprise Support
body:
> **Archived 2025-11-02:** this page is superseded by "Model Switchover & Fallback: Triage Runbook for Enterprise Support" and is kept for reference only.

Summary
-------
This runbook covers triage, model switchover and fallback for enterprise customers (Dedicated or Private) experiencing degraded model behavior, latency spikes or loss of model availability. It is written for Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), SRE on-call and Solutions Engineers supporting a customer-facing incident.

When to use this runbook
-----------------------
Use it when a customer reports any of:
- Token latency (P95 or P99) on generation/chat endpoints above SLA thresholds.
- Persistent quality regressions or hallucinations following a model rollout.
- Model runtime errors (kernel OOMs, model load failures, KV cache corruption).
- Router-triggered automatic fallback that is hurting request success rate.

Preconditions and prerequisites
-------------------------------
Before switching over or falling back:
1. Access: confirm redwood-console access and, where applicable, SSH to the customer's Dedicated/private control plane.
2. Customer configuration: note pinned model version, route policy, cache keys and custom prehooks (Console: Routes > {customer} > {route-id}).
3. SLOs and active incidents on status.redwood-internal. Typical customer SLOs:
   - Latency SLO: P95 < 800ms (hosted) / P95 < 1200ms (dedicated)
   - Error rate SLO: < 1% for 5m window
4. Notify CSE, SRE on-call, Account Manager (AM) and Product (if a model regression is suspected).

Ownership matrix
----------------
- CSE: customer comms, coordination, running this runbook.
- SRE: runtime health checks, switchover commands, rollback safety.
- Solutions Eng: prompt/regression investigation, model/quantization advice.
- Product/Model Ops: suspected model quality regressions (A/B data required).

Immediate triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
--------------------------------------------
1. Capture symptoms: sample requests/responses, timestamps, route-id, model name/version, offtake rate.
2. Health checks from the support workstation:
   - curl -sS -X GET "https://console.redwood/api/internal/health/{route-id}" | jq
   - runbook-utils report-runtime {route-id}
3. Scope: single customer, region or global? Dashboards:
   - Customer route dashboard: /console/dash/{route-id} > Last 60m
   - Global model healthboard: /console/dash/models/{model}

Detailed step-by-step switchover procedure
------------------------------------------
Notify AM and SRE before starting.

1) Prepare the fallback variant
   - Find the approved fallback in Console > Routes > {route-id} > "allowed_models" (commonly "gpt-like-3.5-v2-quant" or "redwood-llm-slim-1.1").
   - Confirm it is loaded on the target cluster:
     rctl --cluster {cluster-name} list-models | grep {fallback-model}
2) Protect the cache (if prefix caching is on)
   - Put the route cache in read-only mode:
     rctl routes update {route-id} --cache-mode read-only --reason "fallback trigger"
3) Switch over (Console or CLI)
   - Console: Routes > {route-id} > Edit > Model > Select {fallback-model} > Save & Canary 10% for 10 minutes.
   - CLI (preferred):
     rctl routes rollout --route {route-id} --to {fallback-model} --strategy canary --canary-size 0.10 --canary-duration 600
4) Watch the canary (10–15 minutes)
   - Latency P50/P95/P99, error rate, success rate, output quality sample set.
   - Promote when latency is back within SLO AND error rate stays below 1% for 10m.
5) Promote or roll back
   - Promote: rctl routes rollout --route {route-id} --promote
   - Roll back: rctl routes rollback --route {route-id} --to {previous-model} --force --reason "canary-fail"

Safety & rollback considerations
--------------------------------
- Do not promote if outputs fail basic safety filters (check safety filter logs).
- If the fallback increases hallucinations or changes SLA-relevant output, escalate to Product and return to the pinned model with throttling.

Quick troubleshooting checklist (error classes)
------------------------------------------------
- High latency with long tails: review batching policy and kernel saturation (top/gpu-top; /usr/local/bin/runtime-inspect --tail-queue on the runtime node).
- OOMs at model load: check quantization variant and free node memory; move to a smaller quantized variant.
- Route-level 5xx: look for 502/504 in router-service logs:
  - kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/router-service --since=10m | grep "{route-id}" | head

Thresholds & quick reference table
----------------------------------
| Metric | Alert threshold | Immediate action | Owner |
| Latency P95 | > 2x SLO for 5m | Start canary to fallback | SRE/CSE |
| Error rate | >= 5% for 5m | Immediate route canary to fallback | SRE |
| Model load failures | any model-load-failure | Disable autoscale, manual load | SRE + Model Ops |
| Safety filter blocks | > 0.5% of responses | Hold promotion, escalate to Product | Product/CSE |

Customer communication templates
--------------------------------
- Acknowledgement: "Thanks for the report. Our SRE and Model Ops teams are triaging now and we will update you within 15 minutes with mitigation steps."
- During switchover: "We are sending a portion of traffic to an alternate model variant to stabilize latency. Responses may differ slightly for a short time."
- Post-incident: brief summary of root cause (if known), actions taken, next steps and postmortem ETA.

Escalation matrix
------------------
1. SRE on-call (primary) — page: SRE-oncall@pagerduty — 0–15m
2. Model Ops (secondary) — page: model-ops@pagerduty — 15–60m
3. Product (quality regressions) — @product-lead — 15–24h
4. Exec/Legal (SLA breach with contractual exposure) — via AM — within 24h

Post-incident actions and RCA requirements
-----------------------------------------
1. Initial incident summary (within 4h) with timeline and mitigation.
2. Full RCA (within 5 business days) with logs, canary graphs, affected request/response samples and preventative measures.
3. Owned, dated action items (e.g., rollback automation, longer canary window).
- Include the incident in the customer QBR (impact, duration, customer severity, planned improvements).

Monitoring playbook
-------------------
- Dashboards: Console > Route Overview ({route-id}); Console > Model Healthboard ({model}); Grafana redwood/request-latency, redwood/error-rate, redwood/model-loads
- Logs: router-service, runtime-agent, model-loader, safety-filter
- Channels: #incidents, SRE-pagerduty, CSE-team slack channel

Related artifacts & links
-------------------------
- Route config schema: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/api-standards/route-config-schema
- Canary rollout CLI reference: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/rollout-cli-usage
- Customer model approval list: Console > Customers > {customer-id} > Approved Models

Appendix: sample CLI snippets
----------------------------
1) 10% canary to the fallback model:
   rctl routes rollout --route r-abc123 --to redwood-llm-slim-1.1 --strategy canary --canary-size 0.10 --canary-duration 600 --reason "support-triage-2025-09-15"
2) Promote after success:
   rctl routes rollout --route r-abc123 --promote
3) Immediate rollback:
   rctl routes rollback --route r-abc123 --to redwood-llm-recent-3.0 --force --reason "rollback-on-failed-canary"

Contact list (internal)
-----------------------
- CSE on-call: cse-oncall@redwood.com
- SRE on-call: sre-oncall@redwood.com
- Model Ops: model-ops@redwood.com
